marta-customer: Hey team — our overnight embedding batch (nightly-emb-03-16) started surfacing lots of 429s around 02:10 UTC. Job id: nightly-emb-03-16. We submit 1024 docs per request, 6 workers x 10 threads = concurrency ~60. Some responses include Retry-After, many don't. Can someone triage? :warning:

lee-support: Sorry you're hitting this. A couple quick Qs: which embedding model are you calling? Are you on a shared project key or a dedicated key? Any recent config changes?

marta-customer: Model string is `text-embedding-3-large` (no explicit version). Using org-shared api key tied to standard plan. No recent client changes. Sample 429 body from our logs:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"error\": \"rate limit exceeded\",
  \"message\": \"burst quota exhausted\"
}
```

sre-bot: We detected a spike originating from that key 02:07:45 -> 02:14:00 UTC. Traffic footprint: ~60 rps at peak, high simultaneous large-batch requests. Shared rate limiter enforces a conservative burst window for non-dedicated keys; that pattern will hit 429 quickly.

omar-ml: note on batch accounting: there is per-request weight plus per-item cost. Very large batches are efficient for tokens/cost but still count towards concurrency/burst. Also, different model variants have different embedding dims: 3-large => 3072, 3-small => 1536. If fallback to a smaller variant happens you may see dimension mismatches.

marta-customer: we started also seeing client-side failures complaining: "vector length mismatch: expected 3072 got 1536". It only shows up intermittently. We didn't change code.

lee-support: two linked causes are likely: (1) burst-triggered routing to a fallback model or (2) a multi-region/alias that maps to different model family. Can you include the raw response body when the shorter vector appears? Also try temporarily pinning the model to an explicit version (e.g., `text-embedding-3-large-v2026-02-01`).

marta-customer: example shorter response we captured:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  \"data\": [[0.001, ... (1536 floats) ... ]]
}
client validation: expected 3072 -> fail
```

omar-ml: yep that matches a 3-small family vector. If you have fallback rules enabled (to keep latency low) the router can temporarily route to a compatible but different-capacity model. That explains the dim flip during the spike.

lee-support: immediate mitigation options:
- Reduce concurrency per worker (try 6-12 total concurrency instead of 60).
- Keep large batch sizes but stagger/phase worker start times so bursts smooth out.
- Implement exponential backoff with full jitter on 429s.
- Pin model version to prevent silent variant routing.

Here's a compact backoff pattern you can plug in (Python-ish):

```
base = 0.6
for attempt in range(6):
    r = call_embeddings()
    if r.status_code == 429:
        wait = base * (2 ** attempt) * random.random()
        time.sleep(min(wait, 30))
        continue
    break
```

marta-customer: reduced concurrency to 12 and phased the 6 workers over 30s. 429s dropped to near zero. The dimension mismatch also stopped. Good catch on routing.

sre-bot: Filing internal incident: INC-2716349001 - "shared-rate-window spike impacting nightly embed jobs". We can also offer a temporary burst increase on your account while you migrate to safer scheduling or evaluate Dedicated.

marta-customer: We'd appreciate a temporary bump while we rework scheduling. Also requesting docs on best-practice for high-throughput offline jobs.

lee-support: Opening quota escalation now and attaching a runbook: suggested steady-state target patterns for offline batches, sample code for jittered starts, and recommended pinning. Will follow up in escalation ticket and mark as P1 for the overnight pipeline.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2716349001 — https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2716349001

omar-ml: longer-term: consider Dedicated for predictable burst/headroom if nightly throughput is business-critical. Also add a runtime check: if embedding vector length != expected, log model string from response and fail fast (avoid silent downstream data corruption).

lee-support: TL;DR playbook for this case:
- short-term: drop concurrency, add jitter/backoff, stagger workers.
- medium-term: pin model versions, instrument vector-dim checks and model-name logging.
- long-term: request Dedicated or quota bump for sustained heavy offline embedding.

marta-customer: thanks all — bump requested. We'll rollout the backoff + staging changes tonight and report back. Appreciate the fast help :clap:
